title: Measured beam-loss reduction from shaped proton distributions at CERN accelerators
summary: At CERN’s Super Proton Synchrotron, resonant excitation reshaped the vertical proton-beam distribution before extraction; the paper reports measured loss reductions up to 23.5%. Surrogate models based on generative deep learning supported rapid validation and Bayesian system identification, with separate measurements at the Proton Synchrotron. A larger reduction described in simulations is an extrapolation and is not presented here as measured performance; an unresolved short-spill surrogate divergence and lack of independent operational replication limit the claim.
ai_technology: A conditional generative deep-learning surrogate maps accelerator settings to beam distributions for rapid validation and system identification; beam-profile shaping itself was experimentally tested.

evidence.tested: The primary v1 reports measured SPS beam profiles and loss-monitor outcomes, surrogate-to-measurement comparison, and separate Proton Synchrotron system-identification measurements.
evidence.unknown: The reported measured reductions are distinct from larger simulated extrapolations. Short-spill surrogate predictions diverged at larger settings for an unresolved reason; independent replication and sustained operational benefit were not shown.
evidence.ai_role: A conditional generative deep-learning surrogate maps accelerator settings to beam distributions for rapid validation and system identification; beam-profile shaping itself was experimentally tested.
